DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City http://w.vw dilg.qgm.ph DILG OPINION No. 100 s. 2021 AUG 05 2021 HON. DONALDO C. SUAREZ Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Quezon Province Dear Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Suarez: This has reference to your letter dated 26 March 2021 requesting this Department's legal opinion on the following matters confronting the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Quezon, thus: 1. Are ex-officio members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan allowed to vote in the reorganization of the same body and its standing committees? 2. Is the reorganization of standing committees of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan attended by only five (5) regular board members, with one (1) acting as the presiding office, valid? 3. Does the installation of Sangguniang Panlalawjgan Administrative Personnel as acting SP Secretariat in the absence of SP Legislative Staff make the subject session void or at least irregular? In reply thereto, we shall answer the foregoing queries in seriatim. Relevant to the first issue is our previous opinion in DILG Legal Opinion NO. 34 series of 2011, dated 11 July 2011 (except the application of the exception to the general rule). In it, we opined in this wise: "[T]he Provincial Councilor's and SK Provincial Federation (SKPF) President acquired their right to sit as ex-officio members of the SP by reason of their having been elected as President of their respective league or federation, whose election thereto also arose originally from their having been elected as Sangguniang Bayan/Panlungsod Membeber, Punong Barangay and SK Chairman, within their respective locality. May we note that the Punong Barangay and SK Chairman are by nature non-partisan local officials. Their non-partisan nature is not

obliterated the moment they are elected as President of their Panlalawigan. This non-partisan character also applies to PCL President since the same assumed the ex-officio membership in the SP in representation, not of his political party (if he belongs to any), but of the federation. Being non-partisan, as a general rule, they should not be considered in the determination of the majority and minority parties in the sanggunian when it comes to the organization/re-organization of the standing committees. This Department has been consistent in its opinion that, as a general rule, ex-officio members of the sanggunian are not allowed to participate and vote in the committee reorganization because the same is based on political party affiliation. Ex-officio members Of the sanggunian are assured of their respective committee chairmanship prescribed under the law. For example, the Liga ng mga Barangay Provincial Chapter President shall automatically hold the chairmanship of the Committee on Barangay Affairs (Article 108 (b) (1) Of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code)." Accordingly, the first query should be answered in the negative. As to the second query, as clearly reflected in the Minutes of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Session dated September 18, 2020, there is a total of thirteen (13) members of the sanggunian, excluding the regular presiding officer. Said Minutes showed that several measures were taken up therein including the reorganization of standing committees. On session day, eight (8) members were present thereby indicating quorum. Of this number, five (5) are regular members (one of them acted as a temporary presiding officer) and three (3) ex-officio ones. With this number, it is clear that reorganization of standing committees would require the affirmative votes of at least five (5) regular members present to pass such measure. Note that while the temporary presiding officer is included in quorum determination, he cannot be counted in the majority vote and participate in the reorganization of the regular committees as his option to vote is contingent and arises only when there is a tie to break. (Javier vs Cadiao, G.R. No. 185369, August 3, 2016). That leaves the sanggunian with four regular members voting in the said reorganization in a session of eight attendees where the needed number to approve this measure is at least five of them. As it was already opined earlier that the three ex-officio members in attendance then are proscribed to vote on matter of committee reorganization, the approval, therefore, of the reorganization of standing committees in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Quezon attended by only five (5) regular board members, with one (1) acting as the presiding officer is questionable. Anent the last query, this Department is of the view that the "installation" or maybe more aptly termed as "designation" of a Sangguniang Panlalawigan Administrative Personnel as acting SP Secretariat in the absence of SP Legislative Staff does not

render the sanggunian session void or irregular as it is immaterial to the validity of the sanggunian session. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Unders etary for Local Government LLLSf27 Copy furnished: DIR. ARIEL O. IGLESIA Regional Director, DILG-Region IV-A Region IV-A (CALABARZON) Address: 3/F Andenson Bldg. 1 National Highway, Brgy. Parian, City of Calamb Laguna
